comparisons.peer_summary: Subordinated debt is generally issued to meet the capital requirements of the Firm or its regulated subsidiaries and is primarily U.S. dollar denominated.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley disclose that subordinated debt is issued to meet capital requirements. Goldman Sachs specifically defines 'Qualifying subordinated debt' for Tier 2 capital purposes as having an original maturity of five years or greater, with the qualifying amount reduced once remaining maturity hits five years. Morgan Stanley broadly states that its subordinated debt is issued to meet the capital requirements of the Firm or its regulated subsidiaries and is primarily U.S. dollar denominated, without specifying the same five-year reduction mechanism in this excerpt.

sentences.text: • Qualifying subordinated debt is subordinated debt issued by Group Inc. with an original maturity of five years or greater. The outstanding amount of subordinated debt qualifying for Tier 2 capital is reduced upon reaching a remaining maturity of five years. See Note 14 for further information about the firm's subordinated debt.
Subordinated debt generally is issued to meet the capital requirements of the Firm or its regulated subsidiaries and primarily is U.S. dollar denominated.
